findings.evidence: Artin.lean:317-327; the criterion `indVirtualCharactersBaseChangeRat_surjective` (Ideal.lean:194) requires only `n ≠ 0` and `∀ f ∈ virtualCharacters k G, n • f ∈ indVirtualCharacters k G P`; `natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic` (Artin.lean:245) and `natCard_nsmul_one_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic` (Artin.lean:184) assume only `Field k`, `Group G`, `Finite G`.
findings.fix: Drop both instance arguments and prove directly: `indVirtualCharactersBaseChangeRat_surjective _ (Nat.card G) Nat.card_pos.ne' fun _ hf ↦ natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic hf`. Update the docstring and the module docstring lines 22-25/46-50, which likewise claim characteristic zero and algebraic closure are needed.
findings.issue: `indVirtualCharactersBaseChangeRat_surjective_isCyclic` assumes `[CharZero k] [IsAlgClosed k]`, both visibly unused: the proof detours `apply indVirtualCharacterSpan_le_indVirtualCharacters` then `rw [← indVirtualCharacters_eq_indVirtualCharacterSpan ...]`, which returns the goal to exactly what it was, and closes with `natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isCyclic hf` (no hypothesis on `k`).

findings.evidence: Artin.lean:354-364 mirrors 317-327; `natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isElementary` (Artin.lean:346) has no hypothesis on `k`.
findings.fix: Drop both instance arguments; prove as `indVirtualCharactersBaseChangeRat_surjective _ (Nat.card G) Nat.card_pos.ne' fun _ hf ↦ natCard_nsmul_mem_indVirtualCharacters_isElementary hf`, and adjust the docstring accordingly.
findings.issue: Same unused assumptions in `indVirtualCharactersBaseChangeRat_surjective_isElementary`: `[CharZero k] [IsAlgClosed k]` are used only by the identical cancelling round trip through `indVirtualCharacterSpan`.

summary: Both rational-surjectivity theorems carry `[CharZero k] [IsAlgClosed k]`, but the hypotheses are used only by a self-cancelling `apply`/`rw ←` round trip through `indVirtualCharacterSpan`; the sharp identity they rest on holds over any field, so the theorems are stated at a strictly weaker level than they prove.
